research_question: Environment gate: does PyTorch see CUDA on the audited GPU?
hypothesis: torch.cuda.is_available() is true on the RTX 4060 Laptop GPU and fp32/fp16 CUDA matmuls are numerically correct
config: isolated smoke test; fp32/fp16/bf16 matmul vs float32 CPU reference; 256x256
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (sm_89, 8187.5 MiB)
peak_vram: 8187.5 MiB total VRAM reported; usage not measured (trivial allocation)
evaluation: PASS (automated numeric check; no human scoring needed)
conclusion: CUDA verified. Relative error 6.32e-07 fp32, 5.22e-04 fp16, 4.28e-03 bf16, all within tolerance. bf16 works, so it is available as a documented fp16 fallback. Driver is 610.88, NOT the 610.74 in the 2026-07-27 audit; it was updated in between. The wheel's bundled CUDA 12.6 runs correctly on a driver advertising CUDA 13.3, confirming nvidia-smi reports the driver's maximum supported API rather than a toolkit PyTorch must match.

research_question: RQ2: is SDXL feasible on 8 GB VRAM at 512 px and at its native 1024 px?
hypothesis: SDXL inference works with memory optimisations but is marginal on 8 GB
config: fp16; DPMSolverMultistepScheduler; guidance 7.5; memory tier 0; no safety checker shipped; frozen kit c40749bc
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (sm_89, 8187.5 MiB)
peak_vram: 512x512: 7859.26 MiB allocated / 9030 MiB reserved / 8187.5 MiB device / 2309.61 MiB RSS. 1024x1024: 10738.08 MiB allocated / 14510 MiB reserved / 8187.5 MiB device / 6806.57 MiB RSS
evaluation: PENDING human rubric scoring at the review gate - no score assigned by the assistant
conclusion: Does NOT fit in 8 GB at native resolution, despite 30/30 runs reporting success - a result that would be misread without the memory figures. At 1024x1024 peak allocated (10738 MiB) and reserved (14510 MiB) both exceed the 8187.5 MiB of physical VRAM: Windows WDDM spilled silently into shared host memory (RSS 6807 MiB) instead of raising a CUDA OOM, so no exception was thrown and memory-tier escalation never triggered. Cost is roughly 29x SD 1.5 per 512 px image and about 118 s per native image. Even at 512 px it saturates the whole device.
next_action: Await Kylian's rubric scores; flag the silent-spill behaviour as a hardware-feasibility finding for risk R1 and for LoRA planning in Prototypes 3-4

research_question: RQ8: how should the ~1:3.6 deck aspect ratio be produced?
hypothesis: Direct tall generation degrades composition; generate-then-crop is more reliable
config: fp16; DPMSolverMultistepScheduler; guidance 7.5; memory tier 0; one strategy per fresh process; frozen kit c40749bc
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (sm_89, 8187.5 MiB)
peak_vram: 512x512 2675.38 MiB allocated; 512x1024 3283.69 MiB; 512x1536 3892.01 MiB; square-crop 2675.38 MiB (identical to 512x512, as expected)
duration: 512x512 median 4.111 s (spread 0.08); 512x1024 median 8.962 s (spread 0.09); 512x1536 median 15.244 s (spread 0.20); square-crop median 4.281 s (spread 0.53)
evaluation: PENDING human composition scoring at the review gate - no score assigned by the assistant
conclusion: 24/24 runs succeeded at tier 0. The hypothesis appears REFUTED on the memory and reliability axes: direct 1:3 generation reached 512x1536 in 3892 MiB, under half the VRAM budget, with no failures. square-crop's real cost is resolution - a 1:3 strip from 512x512 leaves only 170x512 usable pixels, far below deck-print needs. 1:3 is a stated approximation of the true ~1:3.6 because dimensions must be multiples of 64. Composition quality itself is Kylian's to judge. This experiment also produced a measurement-methodology correction: the first run put all four geometries in one process, which contaminated the reserved and device VRAM figures and inflated square-crop to 7.96 s for provably identical work. Thermal throttling was tested and RULED OUT (a hotter, more throttled card ran the same work faster, at 4.10 s); the cause was in-process caching-allocator state, and re-running one strategy per process cut timing spread about 20x.
next_action: Await Kylian's composition scores; adopt one-configuration-per-process for all VRAM and timing measurement in Prototypes 3-5
